pr_title: usb: cdc_acm: Additional connection state checks
pr_body:
Issues caused:
- On intense use I had packet losses (below 1 per 1000)
- Restarting the host device or resetting the USB controller caused the usb transfer to get stuck in about 30% of tests
- This includes issue #72786 opened by a collegue

Analysis of issues:
  I found multiple cases causing this isssues with wrong return values on cdc_acm_irq_is_pending(), cdc_acm_irq_tx_ready() etc causing my logic to get stuck

Changes:
- usb_transfer(): k_work_submit_to_queue() return value was ignored -> calling function tx_work_handler() dropped data even though it was
   not put to workqueue
- tx_work_handler() put dev_data->tx_ready to false even if usb_transfer() failed but without the transfer done callback it was never reset to true so TX got stuck
- cdc_acm_irq_tx_ready() did not check configured and suspended states This caused the device to show as ready even though it was not configured after a host reset
- cdc_acm_irq_rx_ready() did not check if irq is enabled
- cdc_acm_irq_is_pending() had the same issues as its just a test on cdc_acm_irq_rx_ready() or cdc_acm_irq_tx_ready() (the description says so, too) -> Replaced it by a call of both functions for a fast and consistent fix

Tests:
- The host reset issue was tested with a Intel NUC with Windows 11 in an endless reset loop, about 2 times per minute, for 12 hours. The issue no longer applies there
- The host reset issue was also tested on a Linux XUbuntu host with a pyusb device reset script. The issue was tested only manually (at 50% success that was good enough) and does not apply any longer
- Data loss was tested with an echo device and a data generating and checking script. It was also tested with a device generating serialized data (counting up).
- Both showed data loss (about 1 byte per GB, in blocks of multiples of 8). For both test cases the issue no longer applied (tested with more than 1 TB of data) Fixes: #72786

Considerations:
- Changes in cdc_acm.c should not have impact on other code. Return values may show an error that was missed before
- Change in usb_transfer.c may influence more devices The new return value should be in an expected range (0 or negative) so I expect it to work with all other components as well

review_comments: I do not think it is right, whether configured or not, UART device itself can fill data into FIFO, it will also break established expectations.

cdc_acm_irq_tx_ready() is implementation of uart_irq_tx_ready(), where the descriptions is "Check if UART TX buffer can accept a new char", `TX buffer`, it is not `Check if UART controller can transfer a new char`.
Well... but it can't (or at least: won't). It will always return 0 because it will always take zero chars. That's not accepting a new char.

The suspend logic in CDC ACM class implementation itself is not quite right.

Linux will suspend the ttyACM device if device claims to support remote wakeup and there is no data from host to device for some time. The device will be woken up by the host if and only if the host wants to send something. If the device has something to send to host, it is up to device to issue to remote wakeup - and it is what Linux expects the ttyACM device supporting remote wakeup will do.

Please remove "Partially fixes issue https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/72786" from the commit message.

>Packet loss happens on cdc_acm transmission (below 1 per 1000).
Also, restarting the host device or resetting the USB controller
caused usb transfer to get stuck.

Why is this happening? And how does that relate to your changes?

As I say in the initial commit (which I was forced to split and shorten):

usb_transfer() drops data by not checking the return value of k_work_submit_to_queue()
This causes tx_work_handler() to not send the data because it thinks they are in the work queue now. It also thinks the device is occupied but as there is no work queue item it won't get freed again. 

The stuck after reset comes from:
cdc_acm_irq_tx_ready() did not check configured and suspended states 
-> This caused the device to show as ready even though it was not configured after a host reset
The same can happen for RX so I fixed it with it, it's the same issue of ignored state.

Together these cause the issues described in the issue post. 
My changes changed this.

But it is okay to fill/read the UART FIFO (ringbuffer) event if USB device is not configured or suspended.

> Can you please provide k_work_submit_to_queue() return value instead of your own interpretation?

k_work_submit_to_queue() returns any of 3 positive values (0,1,2) if successful in different ways or one of 3 negative values if not. Work queue don't fail often so this error is unlikely, too.

Currently the return value gets ignored so the return value ret in usb_transfer() is unchanged and stays at 0. This causes follow up problems in CDC ACM (and most likely also in other USB devices). 

usb_transfer() returns
"0 on success, negative errno code on fail."
so I have to interpret the queue return values 1 and 2 also as success (0)
If usb_transfer() fails, it disables TX interrupts until bus reset or similar. Instead, error branch should reschedule tx_work with some delay, maybe 1ms.
